docLinks.label: Ley No. 582, Ley General de Educación (Nicaragua, 2006) — full text as published by FAOLEX from the Asamblea Nacional's Normaweb record
UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Nicaragua: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
Terms in Ley 582 are 'personas con habilidades diferentes' and special educational needs
Ley 582 does not name language or speech disorder anywhere
The only communication-specific provision in the law is sign language
existing_identificationCriteria: Educacion Basica Especial is for those whose disability hinders regular learning
existing_serviceModel:
Inclusion in regular classrooms, with complementary personalised attention allowed
25 public special education schools nationally, per the ministry via PEER
Eight diversity resource centres sit inside teacher training colleges
existing_legalEntitlement:
Ley 582 binds public and private schools to include pupils with disabilities
The duty is framed as programme design, not an individual therapy entitlement
existing_funding:
Ley 582 art. 88: the state guarantees each public school its running-cost budget line
Art. 90 bans fees, voluntary quotas or any other payment in state primary and secondary
A school community may still organise economic activities for the school's benefit
Art. 92: the state must fight any economic barrier limiting education
existing_workforce:
Teacher training must include study of Nicaraguan Sign Language
No speech and language therapist role appears in Ley 582

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Guatemala: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
The 1991 education law art. 47 reaches language obliquely (PEER rendering in English)
It covers disabilities 'in their linguistic, intellectual or physical' development
The 2007 law defines needs by curricular disadvantage, not by named condition
existing_identificationCriteria:
2007 special education law: disadvantage and difficulty benefiting from the age group curriculum
Special school placement where needs prevent successful integration into mainstream schools
existing_multilingualProvision:
The 1996 law requires bilingual education in majority-indigenous areas
That duty applies to programmes for pupils with disabilities in rural areas
It is the only explicit multilingual clause found in Guatemalan SEN law
existing_serviceModel:
Resource centres for inclusive education have been rolled out since 2019
The Dirección General de Educación Especial runs them
existing_legalEntitlement: The 1996 disability law gives mainstream access with required support services
existing_funding:
The Educational Inclusion Project is funded by the International Bureau of Education (PEER)
Departmental coordinators also help obtain scholarships for students with disabilities
existing_workforce:
The General Directorate of Special Education has a coordinator in each of the 22 departments
Special education centres in municipalities have trained interdisciplinary teams (PEER)
Departmental special education coordinators give technical help to mainstream teachers (PEER)

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, Guyana — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)

existing_terminology:
The term is special education needs, Anglophone-Caribbean vocabulary
The 2014 Education Bill names persons mute, deaf, blind or otherwise challenged
No developmental language disorder category exists in Guyanese education law
Entitlement hangs on the word communicative in the chief education officer's duty
existing_identificationCriteria:
The school principal decides, with professional staff and the parent
Multidisciplinary assessment is required only if possible
Written parental consent is required before any assessment
existing_multilingualProvision:
Ministry has tried to respond to indigenous communities where English may not be first language
The 2008-13 strategic plan records limited attempts to respond to the language issue
Named example is mother-tongue support such as the Macushi Language project
existing_referralPathway:
School Health Unit screening is the main identification route
A Special Education Unit sits within NCERD and sets policy
A national special education needs coordinator sits in the central ministry
Parents have a right of appeal to the minister
existing_serviceModel:
Dual track: integration into regular schools plus state and private special schools
No speech therapist named in the profile; eligibility includes "communicative" attributes
Least restrictive and most enabling environment "that resources permit", 2014 Education Bill
IEP cost is apportioned between the parents and the ministry
existing_legalEntitlement:
Caveat: PEER calls the 2014 instrument a Bill, and enactment was not verified
The chief education officer must provide a programme for eligible pupils
Eligibility covers intellectual, communicative, behavioural or physical attributes
Delivery must be in the least restrictive environment that resources permit
existing_funding:
Unusual in this region: the cost of an individual education plan is shared
It is apportioned between the parents and the ministry
existing_workforce:
No speech and language therapist role appears anywhere in the national profile
Ministry data: under 40 per cent of special education teachers have sufficient training
existing_outcomesEvidence: Ministry describes special education needs as one of the most neglected areas of the sector

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Honduras: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
SEN, in PEER's English rendering; the Spanish originals were not retrieved
The 2014 resolution: difficulties of varying severity, 'not necessarily due to disability'
No language, speech or communication category is named in the instruments read
existing_identificationCriteria:
Resolution 1365 of 2014 creates a departmental psychopedagogical support team
In PEER's English, that team identifies pupils' needs via diagnostic assessments
existing_serviceModel:
Special education centres support mainstream schools through itinerant teams
The 2014 resolution converts special centres into inclusion resource centres
existing_legalEntitlement:
The 2005 disability equity act guarantees access at all education levels
In both the public and the private systems
existing_workforce: No speech and language therapist role was found in any instrument read

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Panama: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
SEN, in PEER's English rendering; the Spanish originals were not retrieved
The 2006 inclusive education plan defines SEN by difficulty progressing
No language, speech or communication category is named in the instruments read
existing_identificationCriteria:
In PEER's English: SEN assessment is the interdisciplinary team's responsibility
The team is external to the school: psychologists, social workers and teachers
existing_multilingualProvision:
Act 88 of 2010 recognizes indigenous languages and alphabets and regulates bilingual education
MEDUCA must regulate indigenous language use in schools in the comarcas and collective lands
The stated aim is to preserve the native language and promote Spanish and English
existing_serviceModel:
Educational support services operate across thirteen educational regions
The support is described as temporary, advising on plans and proposals
existing_legalEntitlement:
Act 42 of 27 August 1999 requires inclusion with support services and technical aids
Executive Decree No. 1 of 4 February 2000 regulates placement
Priority is given to the mainstream centre nearest the pupil's home
existing_funding: State must allocate funds where family resources are insufficient or access is difficult
existing_workforce:
The support-service staffing list contains no speech and language therapist
It names special education, psychology, social work and learning difficulties

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, Suriname — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)

existing_terminology:
Dutch logopedie is the term that would apply, and it is absent from policy
The 2008 special-education report lists handicaps and behaviour, not language
Suriname has no inclusive education law and no official definition
existing_identificationCriteria: Not established from the sources consulted. PEER records that there is no evidence of an inclusive education law in Suriname and therefore no official definition adopted in the country, so there is no instrument in which criteria could sit. It also records that the country has very limited capacity for early detection of disabilities.
existing_multilingualProvision:
Dutch is the school language while more than 30 languages are spoken nationally
No source addresses distinguishing disorder from Dutch-as-second-language difficulty
existing_referralPathway:
Very limited national capacity for early detection of disabilities
No referral route specific to speech or language was located
existing_serviceModel:
Special schools are concentrated in Paramaribo, 18 of them; five districts have none
The Pedologisch Instituut implements special education programmes nationally
A Health Care Network for Special Education supports pupils who need it
No school-based speech and language service was found
existing_legalEntitlement:
No statutory entitlement: PEER finds no law or policy on inclusive education
The 1987 Constitution Art. 39 guarantees free primary education only
Suriname ratified the CRPD on 29 March 2017
existing_funding:
IBE-UNESCO 2007, via PEER: parents paid extra for special care in private and regular schools
Primary and lower secondary education are free of charge
existing_workforce:
Speech therapists sit on the 2004 National Advisory Board on disability policy
That is a policy body, not a school service; no register or headcount was found
CRC reporting in 2014 found most service providers inadequately trained

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, El Salvador — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)

existing_terminology:
Umbrella term is educacion especial for pupils with special educational needs
Ley General de Educacion defines special education by method, not by category
No speech, language or communication category appears in national policy
Term count on the national inclusion profile: speech 0, language disorder 0
existing_serviceModel:
A Full Time Inclusive School Model was formalised in 2009 after a 2005 pilot
A Department of Inclusive Education sits inside the Ministry of Education
A deputy directorate for the full-time inclusive system was created in 2012
The target is 351 full-time integrated inclusive systems between 2016 and 2026
existing_legalEntitlement:
Special education is free of charge when provided by the state
The 2009 child protection law makes special education free alongside other stages
Placement is in specialised institutions or mainstream centres as needs require
existing_funding:
The CRPD Committee found free state special education was not always the case
The Educated El Salvador Plan proposes incentives for schools and teachers on inclusion
existing_workforce:
No speech and language therapist role appears in national education policy
The ministry has 600 inclusion support teachers for 5,100 public schools
Those teachers serve more than 8,000 pupils with disabilities
existing_outcomesEvidence:
No language-specific figure exists and none can be derived from the school census
18 per cent of disability registrations do not specify the type of disability
2014 school census: 85 per cent of disabled children are in mainstream schools

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, Venezuela (Bolivarian Republic of) — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)

existing_terminology:
Trastornos de lenguaje, one of nine areas de atencion
Specialist training pairs it with hearing, as Deficiencias Auditivas y Lenguaje
Later instruments use necesidades educativas especiales with no language sub-category
Set by a 1976 policy that rejects aetiological categories for a functional profile
existing_identificationCriteria:
Assessment is educational and psychological, producing a functional profile
The stated aim is to stop diagnostic labels prejudicing educational intervention
Placement decisions require a multidisciplinary team
existing_referralPathway:
Centres for diagnosis, guidance and monitoring of disability created in 2011
An interdisciplinary group evaluates the pupil at these centres
153 centres nationwide by 2015, against a stated target of 335
existing_serviceModel:
Special education runs as a modalidad parallel to the basic education subsystem
A 2011 reform converted special schools into Bolivarian and technical schools
The 2013 school inventory lists no school type for language
existing_legalEntitlement:
Resolucion 2005 of 1996 obliges all schools to admit and retain SEN pupils
Ley para Personas con Discapacidad 2007 Art. 16 gives a right to attend
Art. 20 guarantees deaf pupils bilingual education in sign language and Spanish
existing_funding:
Conapdis certification gates the benefits and allowances granted by the social security system
The Constitution makes education free and compulsory (art. 102, read via UNESCO PEER)
The state's 2015 CRPD report claims free support to over 358,000 people with disabilities
existing_workforce:
Specialist teachers, not therapists, are the trained workforce named in policy
Training began in September 1976 at the Instituto Pedagogico de Caracas
